name: Carlos Slim Helu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Mexico's richest person, Carlos Slim Helú and his family control América Móvil, Latin America's biggest mobile telecom firm.
With foreign telecom partners, Slim bought a stake in Telmex, Mexico's only phone company, in 1990. Telmex is now part of América Móvil.
He also owns stakes in Mexican construction, consumer goods, mining and real estate companies. He previously held a 17% stake in The New York Times.
His son-in-law Fernando Romero designed the Soumaya Museum in Mexico City, home to Slim's extensive, eclectic art collection.
Slim and his family own 76% of Grupo Carso, one of Latin America's largest conglomerates.
forbes_facts: Every Sunday, Slim's father would give him a 5-peso allowance and required him to record his purchases in a ledger.
Before going into business, Slim taught algebra at UNAM, a university in Mexico City.

name: Brad Jacobs
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2023); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Most of Brad Jacobs' fortune comes from Greenwich-based QXO, Inc., a publicly traded roofing and building materials company operating in the U.S. and Canada.
Jacobs acquired QXO through a tender offer in 2025, fourteen years after creating the commercial trucking company XPO Logistics.
In 2021, XPO spun off its warehousing business into GXO Logistics, which contracts with retailers to manage inventory and fill orders. In 2022, it spun off its truck brokerage business into RXO.
In the 1990s, Jacobs consolidated rural trash hauling, building United Waste and flipping it to Waste Management in 1997 for $1.9 billion.
He then built United Rentals into the biggest heavy equipment rental company in the world. Its shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
forbes_facts: A trained classical pianist, Jacobs studied piano and mathematics at Brown University before dropping out.
Jacobs has a Palm Beach mansion a few doors down from Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago.

name: Ernest Garcia III
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2021); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2022); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Ernest Garcia III is the cofounder and CEO of Carvana, an ecommerce platform for buying and selling used cars.
Garcia III launched Carvana in 2012 as a subsidiary of DriveTime, a traditional used car business founded and run by his billionaire father, Ernest Garcia II.
Garcia started Carvana as a way to sell used cars directly instead of relying on middlemen; the company also offers financing services.
In 2017, Carvana spun out of Drivetime in an IPO that raised $225 million.
Garcia III's father helped fund the initial development of Carvana and remains its largest shareholder.
forbes_facts: In 2018, Garcia gave $35 million worth of his personal stock to Carvana employees to commemorate the company selling its 100,000th car.

name: Chris Larsen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Chris Larsen cofounded Ripple in 2012 to facilitate international payments for banks using blockchain technology.
Ripple counts American Express and Santander among its 100-plus customers.
Larsen stepped down as Ripple CEO in December 2016 but remains executive chairman.
Prior to Ripple, he cofounded online mortgage lender e-Loan in 1996 and Prosper, a peer-to-peer lender, in 2005.
In April 2019, Larsen and his foundation gave $25 million, largely in XRP, to San Francisco State University.

name: Alain Bouchard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Alain Bouchard cofounded convenience store conglomerate Alimentation Couche-Tard with a single Quebec shop in 1980.
As executive chairman, Bouchard still oversees the $73 billion (sales) company, which boasts more than 17,000 owned or franchised stores worldwide.
Bouchard, who grew the business rapidly by snatching up competitors, retired as president and CEO in September 2014.
Couche-Tard acquired the Circle K chain in 2003 and the Holiday Stationstores and CST Brands chains in 2017.
Couche-Tard made a $20 billion bid for French food retailer Carrefour in early 2021, but the French government nixed the deal.
forbes_facts: Bouchard got his start stocking shelves at his brother's franchised Perrette store and, after climbing the ladder at two chains, struck out on his own.

name: Dinara Kulibaeva
forbes_bio: Dinara Kulibaeva is the daughter of Kazakhstan's former president, Nursultan Nazarbayev, and  shares a majority of Halyk Bank with her husband, Timur Kulibayev.
Their portfolio also includes investments focused on the construction, operation and servicing of oil and gas wells.
She benefited from the 2014 sale of Altynalmas Gold to Polymetal, part-owned by Russian billionaire Alexander Nesis, for cash and company shares.
Forbes assumes all of Kulibaeva's assets are owned 50/50 with Timur, giving them an equal net worth.
Halyk Bank, based in Almaty, Kazakhstan, is their most valuable holding.
forbes_facts: A graduate of Moscow's Institute of Theater Arts, Kulibaeva served as head of the president's education foundation, which supports Kazakh students with financial aid
Timur Kulibayev was on the board of the Russian energy giant Gazprom from 2009 to 2022 and has also held high-level positions in Kazakhstan's oil and gas sector.

name: Charles De Ganahl And David H. Koch
B. Partha Saradhi Reddy
forbes_bio: B.Partha Saradhi Reddy is chairman of  Hetero Group, which he founded in 1993.
Hetero produces a range of anti-retroviral drugs for a host of diseases including AIDS.
It has a portfolio of more than 200 products across therapies ranging from cancer to immunology to diabetes.
Hetero makes branded and non-branded generic medicines.
He is a member of the Rajya Sabha, upper house of the Indian Parliament.
forbes_facts: Reddy has a Ph.D in synthetic organic chemistry from Hyderabad's Osmania University.
Son Vamsi Krishna is managing director of the Hetero Group.

name: Austen Cargill II
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2009-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Austen Cargill II is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, the family business where he served as a vice president until retiring in 2001.
His great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.
Before becoming a Cargill executive, Austen earned a Ph.D. and worked as a marine biologist for the company.
